evidence: books/served-catalog.lisp:2377-2384: `(and (not (consp (fn-scat-number-article group number v fn-arena fn-cat))) (consp (fn-nntp-find-group-number group number (fn-ctl-pin-withdrawn (fn-gidx-pin-control index)))))`. fn-nntp-find-group-number (books/nntp-projection.lisp:83-90) is a linear recursion over a list of articles. This arm runs first in fn-nntp-archive-command-cat (books/served-catalog-dispatch.lisp:59-64) for every by-number retrieval.
fix: Key the withdrawn set by (group, number) in the control pin (a bucket or an index like the number column), or record withdrawal in the catalog row so the miss path is an O(1) lookup. At minimum, give fn-nntp-find-group-number an :exec loop.
reviewer: The linear walk is confirmed: fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p-cat (books/served-catalog.lisp:2372-2384) calls fn-nntp-find-group-number over the pinned withdrawn list whenever the number names no visible article, and dispatch runs this arm first for ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY/STAT by number (served-catalog-dispatch.lisp:59-64). That costs O(W) per miss. The stack-exhaustion claim is refuted: fn-nntp-find-group-number (books/nntp-projection.lisp:83-90) is tail-recursive, since the recursive call is in tail position, so it uses no stack frame per element. What remains is a cost issue on missed number lookups.
scenario: After many cancels or withdrawals, the withdrawn list in the control pin holds W articles. A client probing absent numbers ('STAT 1', 'STAT 2', ... over a sparse range, or a reader skimming expired numbers) pays O(W) per command, and the walk is non-tail recursive in :logic with no :exec loop. That is one stack frame per withdrawn article, the same class of stack exhaustion PKT-877 removed elsewhere.
title: ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY/STAT by number walks the whole withdrawn list on every miss
